profile.reading:
Csquare IAD2-B sits at 22860 International Drive, Sterling, Virginia 20166, part of Csquare's IAD2 campus in Loudoun County. Csquare's own materials describe the IAD2 campus as having two additional pods connected by dark fiber to the nearby IAD1 campus, and this building is one of those two pods, per OSM address tagging cross-referenced against Csquare's IAD spec sheet. Csquare's SEC Form S-1 property table, however, lists only one IAD2 asset, "IAD2_A," treating the whole leased-and-owned IAD2 campus as a single reportable property rather than separately disclosing an "IAD2-B" line item. This building's individual leasing percentage and square footage are therefore not independently broken out in Csquare's SEC filing the way IAD2-A's figures are. Its existence and address are nonetheless confirmed by Csquare's own spec-sheet documentation and this record's OSM sourcing. Csquare, formerly branded Centersquare, was launched in April 2024 by Brookfield Infrastructure to combine Cyxtera, acquired out of Chapter 11 bankruptcy for $775 million in a deal completed January 2024, with Evoque, AT&T's divested data center business held by Brookfield since 2019. Csquare went public via IPO on NASDAQ in July 2026 at $21.00 per share. Csquare's public spec sheet gives a campus-wide total of 48,169 square feet of raised floor, 35.8 megawatts of utility power, 8.5 megawatts of UPS capacity, and 20 megawatts of generator capacity across the IAD2 campus, with SOC 1/2 Type II, PCI-DSS, NIST 800-53 PE High, and ISO 27001 certifications. Csquare does not name a power utility or year-opened date for this campus. Dominion Energy serves Loudoun County as a matter of public record.

Csquare's Sterling, Virginia IAD2 campus sits within Loudoun County's Data Center Alley, the largest concentration of data center capacity in the world. Csquare's SEC S-1 discloses 389 megawatts of total sellable power capacity across its full 64-facility, 21-market portfolio as of March 31, 2026, and the same filing notes the company's legal predecessor entity, BIF III US Aggregator (Delaware) LLC, was formed in May 2018 as a Brookfield Infrastructure Fund III vehicle, well before the 2024 Cyxtera and Evoque combination that produced the assets tracked in this dataset. The dark-fiber link Csquare describes between IAD2 and the nearby IAD1 campus allows customers at either site to interconnect directly without routing traffic through a third-party carrier hotel, a practice common among colocation operators running multiple nearby buildings in the same metro. IAD1 and IAD2 are geographically distinct campuses roughly three miles apart in Sterling, each with its own street address and building set, not two names for a single property, and prospective tenants evaluating IAD2-B should treat campus-wide power and floor-space figures as an upper bound on what any single pod, including this one, can draw.

reading.body:
Centersquare IAD2-B is one of two pods on a single campus in Sterling, Virginia, within Loudoun County's Data Center Alley. The IAD2 campus as a whole publishes 35.8 MW of utility power, 8.5 MW of UPS capacity, and 20 MW of generator capacity across 48,169 square feet of raised floor. The individual power and floor space allocation to IAD2-B alone is not published separately; prospective tenants should treat the campus-wide figures as an upper bound on what this building can draw.

At typical AI training density of 40 kW per rack, the campus-wide 35.8 MW of utility power could support roughly 900 racks as a theoretical maximum across both pods combined. The campus holds SOC 1 Type II and SOC 2 Type II certifications, qualifies for PCI-DSS compliance, meets NIST 800-53 PE High standards, and carries ISO 27001 certification. Dark fiber links IAD2 directly to Centersquare's nearby IAD1 campus, allowing tenants at either site to interconnect without routing through a carrier hotel.

In Virginia, this campus ranks 26th by published power capacity among 330 mapped facilities, with 25 total facilities in the state disclosing megawatt figures. Virginia's published capacity totals 1603.4 MW, placing the IAD2 campus at roughly 2.2 percent of the state's disclosed power. The operator does not publish the year this campus opened or confirm which utility provides power, though Dominion Energy serves Loudoun County as a matter of public record.
